claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state has low hardness and strength.
The alloy's low hardness and strength are governed by nano-scale defect and dislocation-network formation during deformation.
In-situ TEM or synchrotron X-ray diffraction can reveal the proposed defect and dislocation evolution.
Uniaxial tensile deformation causes nano-scale defects and dislocation networks to form.
Formation of nano-scale defects and dislocation networks reduces hardness.
Formation of nano-scale defects and dislocation networks reduces strength.
After tensile deformation, hardness will be 20% lower than in the undeformed starting state.
After tensile deformation, strength will be 30% lower than in the starting state.
Tensile deformation will increase dislocation density relative to the starting state.
Tensile deformation will increase nano-scale defect formation relative to the starting state.
The proposed mechanism applies to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to a simple solid-solution structural state.
The proposed loading boundary is uniaxial tension at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
The primary proposed test condition is room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The role of grain boundaries and precipitates in the deformation behavior and mechanical properties is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The low hardness and strength are properties of the undeformed starting state, but the proposed governing defects and dislocation networks are described as forming only during subsequent deformation. The hypothesis does not establish that these features already exist in the starting state, creating a temporal mismatch between the property being explained and its proposed cause.
